learned: Both machines use a 54 mm portafilter, so any grinder recommendation has to fit 54 mm. Breville lists a '54 mm stainless steel portafilter' for the Barista Express in the US and UK, and Sage lists a '54mm Portafilter' in the Barista Pro's accessories (barista-express/portafilter-54mm, barista-pro/portafilter-54mm-gb).

The Barista Express grinder is an integrated conical burr grinder with 16 settings. The Barista Pro's grinder uses 'Baratza European Precision Burrs with 30 grind settings', so the two built-in grinders are not presented as the same hardware (barista-express/builtin-grinder-16-settings, barista-pro/builtin-grinder-baratza-burrs).

CoffeeGeek's 2023 review says the Smart Grinder Pro's 40 mm burr group is 'the same one that was in the Barista Express espresso machine'. Seattle Coffee Gear's 2016 comparison also found conical stainless burrs like the Smart Grinder Pro's. For an Express owner, Breville's own standalone grinder is the same burr set in a separate box (breville-smart-grinder-pro/burr-group-shared-with-barista-express).

CoffeeGeek calls the Smart Grinder Pro 'a clumpy, clumpy grinder for espresso' that 'retains a lot of grinds' and should 'never, ever' be single dosed (breville-smart-grinder-pro/espresso-limitations-review).

An OzBargain owner told a Barista Express owner that the Smart Grinder Pro 'wont be an upgrade from the built in grinder you have in barista express'. The same thread suggested a DF54 or a Eureka Mignon (breville-smart-grinder-pro/owner-not-an-upgrade).

The Smart Grinder Pro has 60 settings, stainless conical burrs, 0.2-second timed dosing and a 50–54 mm portafilter cradle. In GB it is sold as Sage (breville-smart-grinder-pro/sixty-settings-conical, breville-smart-grinder-pro/portafilter-cradles, breville-smart-grinder-pro/timed-dosing-us).

The Baratza Encore ESP uses 40 mm M2 conical steel burrs and is sold in the US and GB under the same name. Baratza assigns settings 1–20 to espresso and lists an included dosing cup intended for 54 mm portafilters (baratza-encore-esp/burrs-40mm-m2, baratza-encore-esp/espresso-settings, baratza-encore-esp/us-dosing-cup).

The DF54 is a 54 mm stainless flat-burr, stepless single-dose grinder. In Coffeeblog's 2026 review, retention was 0.1 g or less from the third use. The DF54 is sold in the US as the Turin DF54 and in the UK through UK retailers, and the reviewer warns that overseas sellers may ship an EU plug and no UK warranty (turin-df54/burrs-54mm-flat-stepless, turin-df54/retention-review, turin-df54/us-stepless-adjustment, turin-df54/uk-buying-caveat).

One reader says the DF54's dosing cradle is made for 58 mm portafilters, though a 54 mm portafilter can be pushed in and held. Owners of 54 mm Breville machines may need to grind into the cup and transfer the coffee, which Espresso Outlet's single-dose workflow already describes (turin-df54/cradle-58mm-owner-comment, turin-df54/us-single-dose-workflow).

Keep path: Breville documents the adjustable upper burr as an owner feature. Replacement upper burrs depend on the batch date (SP0027464 from PDC 1926, SP0001801 before that) (barista-express/upper-burr-adjustment-documented, barista-express/upper-burr-part-sp0027464, barista-express/upper-burr-part-sp0001801, barista-pro/upper-burr-adjustment-documented).

Breville's own troubleshooting for fast shots lists grind, dose and tamp, not the burrs. Stale beans also make shots run fast, so beans should be ruled out before buying anything (barista-express/troubleshooting-runs-too-quickly, barista-pro/beans-roasted-on-5-20-days).
unknowns: Whether the Smart Grinder Pro shares burrs with the Barista Pro's built-in grinder. Breville says the Pro's grinder uses 'Baratza European Precision Burrs', and no source compares the two. The 'sideways move' argument is therefore only supported for the Barista Express (breville-smart-grinder-pro/burr-group-shared-with-barista-pro is unknown).

No professional test compares the Encore ESP or DF54 head-to-head with the Barista Express or Pro built-in grinder on the same machine. Balance Journal says it tested eight grinders with a stock Barista Express, but we did not read that page. Without such a test, 'better than the built-in grinder' rests on reviewer opinion and owner reports.

Eureka Mignon variants per market (US vs GB names and SKUs, Specialità vs Silenzio availability) are not recorded on those cards, and the cards have empty variant lists. A Mignon pick can't be resolved per market until this is checked.
The DF54 manufacturer's own spec page was not reached (Espresso Outlet and UK retailers returned HTTP 429). Cradle fit with a 54 mm Breville portafilter rests on one reader comment.

The Baratza Encore ESP US page re-read on 2026-11-24 did not show the dosing-cup size that the 2026-11-21 read recorded (54 mm plus 58 mm adapter). The GB page doesn't state it either. The content may be dynamic, so this needs a re-check against the manual.
The Barista Express Impress (BES876) was not researched. Its grinder and burr relationship to the Express is unverified, so the guide shouldn't extend Express-specific claims to it.
No current prices were recorded. Prices are per-market merchant data and must not appear in the post text.

competitors.says: Says to upgrade the grinder first (FAQ: 'Upgrade the grinder first') and names the Mignon Silenzio, Sette 270, Mignon Specialità and Niche Zero. Its Quick Answer contradicts this by saying to upgrade the machine first. It never mentions the inner or upper burr adjustment or the Smart Grinder Pro, and it has no keep-what-you-have path.

UK price-tier list (per search snippet; the page was not read in full). It recommends the Mignon Specialità for most people, the Niche Zero as the premium pick and the Sage Smart Grinder Pro as the 'lowest-friction' option. It misses that the Smart Grinder Pro uses the same burr group as the Express's built-in grinder, and it skips diagnosis.

2016 retailer comparison. It found the Express burrs are 'conical stainless steel like the Smart Grinder Pro' and recommends the Smart Grinder Pro if you brew more than espresso. It names no winner for espresso and is dated.
